text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Finance Ministry plans to reform the way funds from the state budget are distributed to local authorities, which will receive some income tax (IRS) revenues.
- According to a preliminary bill on local finances, presented by Finance Minister Antonio de Sousa Franco, a fund will be established to assist projects in Madeira and Azores.
- An agreement signed between the state and retail group Sonae, under which Sonae will buy bankrupt tourist firm Torralta, says the government will pay costs related to the layoff of excess workers.
- A farmers' association said it would be hard to sell all of this year's relatively high output of apples and pears because of competition from the Spanish market.
- Some workers fired by a Grundig car radio factory in Braga in northern Portugal ended their hunger strike after the local mayor promised them jobs.

- Airports company ANA - Aeroportos e Navegacao Aerea has chosen two banks, Banco Fomento e Exterior and Banco Cisf, to assess its value and make recommendations on a restructuring as part of plans to eventually privatise trhe company.
- Portuguese state electricity company EDP - Electricidade de Portugal plans to take a 10 percent stake in the planned 8.5 billion escudos Colon-Solar natural gas-fired power plant in Spain.
